question:
In Vector Database Internals, what failure mode triggers the following observed symptom?
"Edge case trigger: 'Root Cause'"

options.text: Post-filtering ANN search. The HNSW index traverses the top-10 nearest neighbors in vector space, and then discards 9 of them because they fail the metadata filter!
The IVF index selects the centroid farthest from the query vector at search time instead of the nearest one, scanning the one partition guaranteed not to contain the true neighbors.
The metadata filter is applied before the vector search even runs, so the ANN graph never sees the pre-filtered candidate set and returns empty.
The HNSW index was built with ef_construction set far too low, so its graph has too few edges to reach most of the legal documents at all.

explanation: Diagnostic Analysis: Post-filtering ANN search. The HNSW index traverses the top-10 nearest neighbors in vector space, and then discards 9 of them because they fail the metadata filter!

In Vector Database Internals, what failure mode triggers the following observed symptom?

options.text: Use single-stage filtered graph traversal (e.g. Qdrant / pgvector) where filtering bitsets restrict the neighbor traversal candidates during graph traversal.
Have both insert-time and query-time partition lookups call the same nearest-centroid function so they can never drift apart.
Raise the ANN search's top-k parameter from 10 to 1,000 so more candidates survive the metadata filter.
Move the metadata filter into a post-processing step that runs after the full unfiltered result set has already been ranked.

options.text: Query with metadata filter {"category": "legal"} returns only 1 result, even though 10,000 legal documents exist in the database.

Every query against the filtered index returns zero results at all, regardless of how many documents match the filter.
Query latency for filtered searches is identical to unfiltered searches, but recall for the unfiltered case is measurably worse.

question: In 03 Vector Database Internals, what architectural invariant is critical for maintaining high retrieval fidelity?

options.text: Ensuring index synchronization and embedding dimensional alignment for 03 vector database internals.
Applying metadata filters only after the ANN graph traversal has already selected its fixed top-k candidate set.
Using a different nearest-centroid comparison at query time than the one used when vectors were originally inserted into their partitions.
Sizing the HNSW graph's construction parameters for indexing speed alone, without regard to how many edges a query-time traversal can reach.

explanation: Retrieval accuracy requires maintaining strict index synchronization and embedding integrity in 03 vector database internals.
